headline: Bitcoin slipped toward $63,700 on Tuesday as tech stocks fell ahead of Nvidia's results, which land in the early hours of Wednesday Bangkok time, while fear stays extreme and markets bet on a December Fed rate rise.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips toward $63,700 as tech stocks fall ahead of Nvidia's results
stories.summary: Bitcoin dropped about $1,000 in half an hour on Tuesday as US tech stocks sold off. Crypto has been moving together with AI and tech shares, so results from Nvidia, the AI chip maker, after the US close are the next big test. Talk of more Fed rate rises adds pressure, because higher rates make risky assets less attractive.
points: Bitcoin fell about $1,000 in 30 minutes to $64,000 as the Nasdaq fell 1.5% and the S&P 500 1.25%, per CoinDesk; its ticker later showed $63,725.73.
Nvidia reports after the US close, with its call at 5pm ET (05:00 Wednesday Bangkok), per Nvidia. Kiplinger puts the forecast at $108.7B revenue and $2.47 a share.
Former CEO Jensen Huang said he would be 'honored' to return if the board agrees, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, per Kiplinger.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said several rate rises will likely be needed, per CoinDesk. CME FedWatch showed 95.7% odds of a quarter-point rise in December late on 16 Nov UTC, per TechFlow citing Jin10. These are market bets, not a Fed decision.

stories.title: Anthropic's share sale expected to price at or above the top of its range
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic is about to sell shares on the stock market for the first time. It matters for crypto because some analysts say big events like this, plus rate-rise worries, are pulling buyers' money away from crypto.
points: Anthropic told investors it expects to price near the top of its $70-78 range or above it, per Bloomberg reported by CoinDesk.
At $78 a share that would value the company at about $1.4 trillion, per CoinDesk.
The order book closes at 4pm ET Tuesday and was reportedly about six times oversubscribed, per KuCoin News.
Pricing is expected on 18 Nov and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on 19 Nov, per KuCoin News. Not confirmed by the company.

stories.title: CFTC orders Kalshi to stop listing bets on what Trump will say
stories.summary: The CFTC, the US derivatives regulator, ordered the betting platform Kalshi to stop offering contracts on words President Trump might say. It shows the regulator is willing to step in on products popular with everyday users.
points: Kalshi confirmed it is complying with a CFTC order to stop listing 'mention' contracts on Trump's public remarks, per CoinDesk.
Kalshi says the order was aimed at it specifically; it is unclear whether other platforms got similar orders, per CoinDesk.
In September the CFTC warned that mention contracts may be 'presumptively readily susceptible to manipulation', per CoinDesk.
The same day, the Senate Agriculture Committee held a hearing on CFTC nominees Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland, per Coincub.

briefs.title: Stablecoin supply shrinking
briefs.summary: The combined supply of USDT, USDC, BUSD and DAI fell 5% in 30 days to $250B, down from a $273B peak in May; Glassnode calls it one of the largest contractions on record, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Coinbase Borrow reaches New York
briefs.summary: New Yorkers can now borrow USDC against their crypto on Coinbase after state approval, completing the rollout to all 50 states, per The Block.

briefs.title: Ether funds keep losing money
briefs.summary: US spot ether ETFs have seen $772.5M of net withdrawals in November through 16 Nov, per Farside data reported by crypto.news.

briefs.title: Ex-Robinhood engineer pleads guilty
briefs.summary: A former Robinhood engineer pleaded guilty to wire fraud for trading ahead of Robinhood's crypto listing announcements, per The Block.

briefs.title: Strategy to leave MSCI indexes
